public_rationale: Independent FT reporting corroborates an attributable net loss of roughly $39 billion from audited figures. That supports the approximate $38.5 billion claim on the accounting measure specified by the surrounding text. It does not establish an equivalent cash outflow.
limitations: The conclusion relies on independently verified news reporting because the underlying statements were not accessible.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: According to audited financial documents, OpenAI lost around $38.5 billion in 2025.

statement.excerpt: Today, I can exclusively report, based on audited financial documents viewed by this publication that have been independently verified by the Financial Times, that OpenAI lost around $38.5 billion in 2025, as well as other crucial details about the financial condition of the company.
statement.document_title: Exclusive: OpenAI Losses Increased Nearly 8X in 2025, With Spending Hitting $34 Billion

from_speaker: independently verified by the Financial Times
our_interpretation: The surrounding text identifies the measure as net loss attributable to OpenAI after allocating losses to noncontrolling interests.
This is a statement about accounting loss, including noncash charges, rather than cash burn.
The accounting basis is company_reported because Zitron purports to quote company financial statements. Audited does not by itself identify GAAP or IFRS.
The word around permits corroboration reported at a coarser precision, provided the accounting measure matches.
criteria.support_condition: Audited company accounts, or independent reporting verifying those accounts, establish an approximately $38.5 billion net loss attributable to OpenAI for calendar 2025.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable verified accounts establish a materially different attributable net loss, or establish that the stated figure represents a different accounting measure.
